scope_limits: The source compiler uses one existing cubic multiplication for three dynamic base-times-extension products within sufficiently long PCS opening-reduction rows. Three additions remain ordinary instructions, reducing a six-instruction source term to four. Constant and duplicate-lane cases retain scalar folding and CSE.

The recursion lowerer removes a cubic product only when both off-axis operand components come from immutable zero Constant operations, all three outputs have one use, and the three accumulator additions consume the outputs in matching component order. A zero witness never establishes these conditions.

The ordinary MachineAir and the typed recursion AIR are both checked against the scalar reference. Tests cover active and inactive slots, external uses of each product component, permuted components, non-base operands, short chains and parent opening bindings.

The initial prototype applied compaction to all extension scaling. Its twelve-leaf proof verified and CPU compilation was faster, but unrelated scales grew the cubic table from 32768 to 65536 rows. The final source restricts compaction to opening-reduction rows of at least five values, leaving at least four terms after the identity-weight term folds away.

The initial one-proof screen is not a matched three-proof pipeline comparison and does not measure the final narrower implementation. Its timings and geometry are retained as intermediate evidence only.

No GPU kernel, AIR relation, field arithmetic, hash round, transcript, randomness policy, query count, blowup or memory allowance changed. This implementation does not replace the previously documented complete-tree soundness and zero-knowledge review.
No fresh complete N3/N4 aggregation or transaction-generation latency was measured. Linux OpenCL validation does not qualify CUDA or macOS.
